questions.cardText:
[Zoology] Why do flies “rub their hands together” after landing on something?
A. To attract mates
B. To clean themselves
C. To cool down
Answer: B. Flies rub their front legs together to clean off dirt and debris because their legs are covered with taste sensors. Keeping them clean allows flies to better sense their environment and locate food. This is similar to how we clean our glasses to see more clearly.
questions.de: Warum reiben Stubenfliegen ihre Beine aneinander, wo doch an ihren Füßen Geschmacksrezeptoren sitzen?
questions.en: Why do houseflies rub their legs together, given the taste receptors on their feet?
questions.answerDe: Um sie zu putzen (damit die Geschmacksrezeptoren wieder frisch schmecken)
questions.answerEn: To clean them (so the taste receptors work afresh)

timeline.labelEn: A study of the taste receptors on the housefly's feet (tarsal chemoreceptors) is published
timeline.labelDe: Eine Studie über die Geschmacksrezeptoren an den Füßen der Stubenfliege (Tarsal-Chemorezeptoren) erscheint

questions.notes: Wikipedia: houseflies clean their legs by rubbing them together, enabling the chemoreceptors to taste afresh. Timeline = 1935 tarsal chemoreceptor paper cited there.

questions.cardText:
[Chemistry] What is a lipid?
A. A type of protein
B. A type of fat
C. A type of carbohydrate
Answer: B. Lipids are a diverse group of organic compounds. They are fatty acids or their derivatives and are insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents.
questions.de: Welche große Klasse organischer Verbindungen, unlöslich in Wasser, aber löslich in unpolaren organischen Lösungsmitteln, umfasst Fette, Wachse, Sterole und Phospholipide?
questions.en: What broad class of organic compounds, insoluble in water but soluble in nonpolar organic solvents, includes fats, waxes, sterols and phospholipids?

timeline.labelEn: French pharmacologist Gabriel Bertrand introduces the term 'lipide'
timeline.labelDe: Der französische Pharmakologe Gabriel Bertrand führt den Begriff „lipide“ ein

questions.notes: Card's answer is backwards: fats are one kind of lipid, not the other way round (lipids also include waxes, sterols, fat-soluble vitamins, phospholipids). Asked as the class.
